controls.description: Physical access to warehouse and high-value storage areas is restricted to authorised personnel, with access rights reviewed periodically.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Access authorisation lists; key/card issuance logs; periodic access-right reviews signed off by management.
controls.limitations: Does not detect theft by authorised personnel; can be overridden by collusion or management override.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Independent physical inventory counts are performed periodically and differences between counted quantities and inventory records are investigated and approved before adjustment.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Count sheets, reconciliation of counts to records, investigation notes and approved adjustment journals.
controls.frequency: Periodic (e.g. cycle counts or annual full count)
controls.limitations: Only detects losses at the count date; ineffective if counters are not independent or differences are written off without investigation.
controls.objective: Detect unrecorded inventory losses and ensure records agree with physical quantities.
controls.responsible_role: Finance / internal audit, independent of warehouse custody
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Physical count sheets or test counts that disagree with listed quantities.
evidence.description: The detailed listing of inventory quantities (and values) by item and location as at the reporting date.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Complete item/location coverage; footed totals; identifiable as at the reporting date.
evidence.limitations: Internally generated; does not by itself prove existence or condition.
evidence.name: Inventory listing (detailed inventory records)
evidence.reliability_notes: Reliability depends on the effectiveness of inventory record-keeping controls. Because the factor indicates weak physical controls, the listing is treated as the item under test rather than as corroboration of existence.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Unreconciled differences or stale unexplained items.
evidence.description: Reconciliation of the inventory listing total to the general ledger inventory balance, with supporting detail for reconciling items.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Signed/prepared by client staff, dated, with explanations for all reconciling items.
evidence.limitations: Agreement proves arithmetic consistency, not existence.
evidence.name: General ledger reconciliation
evidence.reliability_notes: Auditor-performed footing and agreement increases reliability; reconciling items still require vouching.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Auditor test counts that differ materially.
evidence.description: The entity's count sheets recording quantities counted, counters' identities, and count dates/locations.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Sequentially controlled sheets, counters identified, supervisor sign-off, dated.
evidence.limitations: Does not prove the count was performed properly; auditor attendance or reperformance addresses this.
evidence.name: Physical count sheets
evidence.reliability_notes: More reliable where counters were independent of custody and sheets show evidence of review; weakened where the security factor suggests poor count discipline.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Entity count sheets showing different quantities for the same items.
evidence.description: The auditor's independent record of items and quantities test-counted in both directions.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Independently recorded at the time of counting, identifying item, location, quantity and direction of test.
evidence.limitations: Covers only the items tested; projection to the population requires appropriate sampling discipline.
evidence.name: Auditor test-count records
evidence.reliability_notes: High reliability for existence/completeness of the items tested: obtained directly by the auditor through observation and inspection.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Access logs showing movements with no corresponding movement document.
evidence.description: Documents evidencing movements of inventory into and out of the warehouse around the count date and year-end.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Sequential numbering, dates, quantities, authorisation signatures.
evidence.limitations: Only proves recorded movements; unrecorded movements are the residual risk.
evidence.name: Inventory movement reports (goods received / dispatch notes)
evidence.reliability_notes: Pre-numbered, sequentially controlled documents are more reliable; reliability falls if movements can occur without documentation - which the security factor makes more likely.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Material count differences with no corresponding adjustment.
evidence.description: Journal entries recording inventory shortages, damage, shrinkage and related write-downs, with supporting schedules.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Approved by someone independent of custody, dated in the correct period, supported by count differences or damage reports.
evidence.limitations: A journal proves an entry was made, not that the underlying loss occurred.
evidence.name: Adjustment journals for shortages and losses
evidence.reliability_notes: Reliability depends on independent approval and supporting evidence; unsupported journals are a fraud risk indicator, not proof of loss.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Movement documents for times with no corresponding access record.
evidence.description: Access logs, key/card registers or entry records showing who entered storage areas and when.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Chronological, identifying the person and time; no unexplained gaps.
evidence.limitations: Proves recorded access only; tailgating or unlogged entry points leave no trace.
evidence.name: Warehouse access records
evidence.reliability_notes: System-generated logs are more reliable than manual sign-in sheets; any log can be incomplete if access can bypass the logging point.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Documents that contradict the explanation given.
evidence.description: Management explanations for count differences and the corroborating documents obtained for them.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Documented promptly, attributed, and tied to specific supporting documents.
evidence.limitations: Explanations without corroboration do not resolve a difference.
evidence.name: Explanations and supporting documents for discrepancies
evidence.reliability_notes: Inquiry alone is weak evidence; reliability comes from corroboration with independent or documentary evidence.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

factor_risk.additional_info_needed: Whether inventory is material; whether a physical count is performed at or near year-end; whether perpetual inventory records are maintained.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies where inventory is held on the entity's premises. Less applicable where inventory is held entirely by third parties under independent custodial controls, or where inventory is immaterial.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: Established audit practice: physical safeguarding is a basic control over inventory existence; its absence is a recognised indicator of heightened existence risk.
factor_risk.explanation: Inadequate physical security removes the primary preventive barrier against unauthorised removal of goods. Without restricted access and movement records, losses can occur and remain undetected, so recorded quantities may exceed quantities actually held.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factor_risk.trigger_condition: Physical inventory exists and is material, and warehouse access is not adequately restricted, monitored or logged.

factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where the entity holds physical inventory that is material to the financial statements and the warehouse relies on physical access controls rather than (or in addition to) system controls.
factors.description: Physical inventory is stored in a warehouse where access is not adequately restricted, monitored or logged. Doors, cages or high-value areas are left unsecured, and movements of goods in and out are not consistently recorded or supervised.
factors.name: Inventory held in a warehouse with inadequate physical security
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factors.warning_signs: Unexplained shrinkage between counts; damaged or resealed packaging; inventory movements outside working hours; missing or incomplete goods movement logs; staff reporting unescorted visitors in storage areas.

procedure_evidence.notes: Reconciliation is the output of this procedure.
Count sheets identify what was counted and by whom.
Auditor's own record of items inspected.
Listing is the starting point for listing-to-floor tests.
Test-count records are the primary output.
Explanations and their corroboration are the evidence for resolved differences.
Adjustment journals are the population vouched.
Count sheets support the quantities adjusted.
Movement documents corroborate whether access related to valid movements.
Aggregated findings and conclusions are documented here.

procedures.exception_criteria: Unreconciled differences; reconciling items that are unsupported, stale, or recorded in the wrong period.
procedures.expected_result: The inventory listing reconciles to the general ledger balance; reconciling items are valid, supported and recorded in the correct period.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate the cause of each unreconciled difference; quantify the potential misstatement; consider whether the difference indicates a breakdown in inventory record-keeping that warrants extended procedures.
procedures.objective: Confirm that the detailed inventory records agree with the general ledger balance that feeds the financial statements.
procedures.population: Full inventory listing and general ledger inventory accounts.
procedures.sampling_notes: No sampling - this is a full-population reconciliation.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Obtain the inventory listing (or inventory sub-ledger) as at the reporting date.
Foot and cross-foot the listing and agree the total to the general ledger inventory balance.
Investigate and obtain explanations for reconciling items; verify they are valid and recorded in the correct period.
procedures.title: Reconcile the inventory listing to the general ledger

procedures.exception_criteria: Items selected cannot be located; significant quantities appear damaged or obsolete without segregation; count procedures are not followed.
procedures.expected_result: Selected items exist, are in the expected location and condition, and count procedures appear to have been followed.
procedures.follow_up: Extend inspection to additional items; discuss findings with management; evaluate whether condition issues require valuation adjustments and whether count reliability is impaired.
procedures.objective: Obtain direct evidence of the existence and condition of inventory at the count date.
procedures.population: Inventory on hand at the count date.
procedures.sampling_notes: Select items across locations and value strata, with emphasis on high-value and portable items given the security factor.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Attend the entity's physical inventory count (where appropriate) and observe whether count procedures are followed.
Select a sample of inventory items and inspect their physical existence and condition.
Note the condition of storage, segregation of damaged or obsolete items, and any restrictions on access observed during attendance.
procedures.title: Attend the physical inventory count and inspect selected items

procedures.exception_criteria: Material unexplained differences in either direction; items on the floor not in the listing; listed items not on the floor.
procedures.expected_result: Test counts agree with the listing and count sheets, subject to individually investigated differences.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate each difference with warehouse staff; inspect movement records around the count date; if differences are material and unexplained, extend test counts and reassess the risk assessment for inventory.
procedures.objective: Test both the existence of recorded inventory and the completeness of inventory records.
procedures.population: Inventory listing and physical inventory on hand.
procedures.sampling_notes: Two-directional sample; bias selection toward high-value, portable items and locations with the weakest access controls.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: From the inventory listing, select items and trace to their physical location (listing to floor) - tests existence.
From the warehouse floor, select items and trace back to the inventory listing (floor to listing) - tests completeness of records.
Record quantities independently and compare with both the listing and the entity's count sheets.
procedures.title: Perform two-directional test counts

procedures.exception_criteria: Material unexplained shortages; explanations without supporting evidence; a pattern of differences concentrated in high-value or portable lines.
procedures.expected_result: Each material difference is explained by valid, supported causes (e.g. timing of movements, data entry errors since corrected) and correctly adjusted.
procedures.follow_up: Quantify the potential misstatement; consider extended procedures over the affected lines or locations; evaluate fraud risk indicators - do NOT automatically conclude fraud has occurred; document the basis for the conclusion.
procedures.objective: Determine the cause of count differences and whether adjustments are required.
procedures.sampling_notes: Census of material differences; professional judgment for the materiality threshold.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Obtain the entity's count-to-record reconciliation and identify material differences.
For each material difference, inspect supporting documentation (movement records, dispatch notes, receiving reports).
Discuss unexplained differences with warehouse and finance personnel and document explanations with corroborating evidence.
procedures.title: Investigate material differences between physical counts and inventory records

procedures.exception_criteria: Missing movement records; movements recorded in the wrong period; unrecorded dispatches or receipts.
procedures.expected_result: Movements are completely recorded in the correct period; the count reconciles to the reporting-date balance.
procedures.follow_up: Quantify cut-off errors and propose adjustments; if movement records are systematically missing, extend testing and reconsider reliance on the entity's records.
procedures.objective: Verify that movements around the count date are completely and accurately recorded so the count can be rolled forward or back to the reporting date.
procedures.population: Inventory movements in the window around the count date and year-end.
procedures.sampling_notes: Focus on the last/first movements of the period and on high-value items.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Obtain goods received notes and dispatch/delivery notes for a window around the count date.
Trace a sample of movements to the inventory records and vice versa.
Verify cut-off: movements before the reporting date are recorded in the correct period.
procedures.title: Inspect inventory movement records around the count date

procedures.exception_criteria: Unsupported or unapproved adjustments; adjustments recorded in the wrong period; losses netted or misclassified to obscure shrinkage.
procedures.expected_result: Adjustments are supported, approved, recorded in the correct period and correctly classified.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate the business rationale for unsupported adjustments; quantify misstatements; consider whether the pattern indicates unrecorded losses elsewhere.
procedures.objective: Verify that recorded inventory adjustments are valid, supported and correctly classified.
procedures.population: All inventory adjustment journals in the period.
procedures.sampling_notes: Census of material adjustments; sample smaller ones if numerous.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Extract all journals adjusting inventory for shortages, losses, damage or shrinkage in the period.
Inspect supporting documentation for each material adjustment.
Verify the accounting treatment: losses recognised in the correct period and classified appropriately (not netted against unrelated gains).
procedures.title: Review adjustment journals relating to shortages and losses

procedures.exception_criteria: Evidence of unauthorised access; after-hours movements without supporting dispatch records; missing or tampered logs.
procedures.expected_result: Access is limited to authorised personnel; unusual movements are explained and supported by valid dispatch or transfer documentation.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate each anomaly with management; trace the related inventory; if unauthorised movements are confirmed, extend physical verification procedures and reassess fraud risk - without presuming fraud.
procedures.objective: Obtain evidence about who accessed inventory areas and whether movements were authorised.
procedures.population: Warehouse access records for the period.
procedures.sampling_notes: Targeted review for anomalies rather than statistical sampling.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Obtain access logs, key registers or entry records for the warehouse for the period (where available).
Identify unusual patterns: after-hours access, access by personnel without a business need, gaps in sequential logs.
Corroborate unusual movements with goods movement records and dispatch documentation.
procedures.title: Inspect warehouse access records and investigate unusual movements

procedures.exception_criteria: Aggregate unadjusted differences approach or exceed materiality; findings contradict the original risk assessment.
procedures.expected_result: Findings are individually and in aggregate immaterial, or proposed adjustments have been recorded; the risk assessment remains appropriate.
procedures.follow_up: Propose adjustments to management; if refused, evaluate the impact on the audit opinion; update the risk assessment and extend procedures where the original assessment is no longer supported.
procedures.objective: Conclude on the financial statement impact of all inventory findings taken together.
procedures.sampling_notes: Not applicable - this is an evaluation step.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Aggregate all unadjusted differences, cut-off errors and unsupported adjustments identified.
Assess whether, individually or in aggregate, they indicate material misstatement of inventory or related accounts.
Determine whether additional audit procedures are needed and document the conclusion and its effect on the risk assessment.
procedures.title: Evaluate whether discrepancies require accounting adjustments or additional procedures

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where recorded inventory quantities are material. Existence is the primary assertion affected by unrecorded physical loss.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: If inventory has been stolen or removed without authorisation and the loss is not recorded, the quantities shown in the financial statements include goods that no longer exist.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where the entity is expected to record shrinkage, damage or write-downs; completeness of the loss records is at risk, not completeness of the inventory balance itself.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Losses, shortages and damage that have occurred may not be recorded at all - the population of inventory loss/adjustment entries may be incomplete.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant only where shortages or damage are identified or suspected; valuation adjustments follow from the physical findings, they are not assumed.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Unrecorded shortages or damage affect the carrying amount: damaged or missing items may need write-down, and persistent shrinkage may indicate net realisable value or obsolescence issues.

risk_controls.explanation: Directly addresses the factor: restricting and monitoring access reduces the opportunity for unauthorised removal.
Detects losses that preventive controls failed to stop; the investigation step is what converts a count difference into a recorded adjustment.

risk_procedures.reason: Establishes the baseline: the detailed records that will be tested against physical reality must first agree with the ledger.
Direct observation of existence and condition at the count date.
Two-directional testing covers both existence (recorded items exist) and completeness (physical items are recorded).
Differences are where unrecorded losses hide; each material difference must be explained with evidence.
Roll-forward/back reliability depends on complete movement records around the count date.
Tests that recorded losses are genuine and correctly treated - the completeness assertion for loss records.
Directly targets the factor: whether access was controlled and movements authorised.
Concluding step: aggregates findings and tests whether the risk assessment still holds.

risks.causes: Unrestricted physical access to storage areas; absence of segregation between custody of inventory and record-keeping; weak or unenforced goods movement procedures; collusion or opportunistic theft.
risks.description: Inventory may be stolen, lost or removed without authorisation, or damaged without the loss being recorded. If such losses are not identified and recorded, inventory quantities in the accounting records will exceed quantities actually held.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: Risk increases with the portability and resale value of inventory, the number of people with access, and the absence of perpetual records. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.
risks.potential_consequences: Inventory may be overstated if losses are not recorded. Inventory records may not agree with physical quantities. Losses may be incorrectly classified or omitted from the accounts.
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
risks.title: Inventory loss through theft, unauthorised removal or unrecorded damage

rules.name: Inadequate warehouse security -> inventory loss risk
rules.rationale: Unrestricted physical access removes the main barrier to unauthorised removal of goods, so recorded quantities may exceed quantities actually held. The rule directs the auditor to existence-focused substantive procedures and to test the completeness of loss records, with explicit per-assertion reasoning.
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

missing_information: Whether inventory is material to the financial statements.
Whether a physical count is performed at or near the reporting date, and whether the auditor can attend.
Whether perpetual inventory records are maintained.
then.note: Physical safeguarding is the primary preventive control over inventory existence; its absence elevates existence risk and requires direct substantive evidence (observation, test counts) rather than reliance on records.
